results.model_answer: The network replaces any protocol configuration options IE or extended protocol configuration options IE previously received during attach procedure execution with those included in the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.6.1.2.4: "A protocol configuration options IE or extended protocol configuration options IE included in the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message replaces any ... previously ... received during the attach procedure execution."

results.question: If a UE in the EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE substate has its USIM removed, what is the resulting substate? Conversely, what condition would cause a UE in EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE to transition to EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTACH-NEEDED?
results.reference: If the USIM is removed from a UE in EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE, the UE enters substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-IMSI. A UE in EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE would transition to EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTACH-NEEDED if valid subscriber data are available but an attach must be performed as soon as possible, for example, if the access class is blocked due to access class control or if the network rejects the NAS signalling connection establishment.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.3.8, eCALL-INACTIVE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.3.7, EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTACH-NEEDED
results.model_answer: USIM removal causes EMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE to transition to EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-IMSI. From EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE, the UE transitions to the attach-needed/EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH substate when an attach is required, e.g. a network-requested re-attach or an upper-layer request requiring EPS service/attachment.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 5.2.2.3.8: 'if the USIM is removed, the UE enters substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-IMSI'. For attach, clause 5.2.2.4 states: 'If an attach shall be performed (e.g. network requested re-attach), the substate shall be ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH.'

results.question: For a UE in WB-S1 mode requesting a PDN connection that is not for UAS services and with a PDN Type other than non-IP/Ethernet, which IE related to protocol configuration options should be included if the UE wishes to transmit data to the network and end-to-end ePCO support is not present?
results.reference: The Protocol Configuration Options IE (Clause_8_3_20_4) shall be included. This clause explicitly states the inclusion conditions for this scenario (UE in WB-S1 mode, PDN Type not non-IP/Ethernet, APN not for UAS services). It also states this IE shall not be included if the Extended Protocol Configuration Options IE is included, which aligns with the general rule in Clause_6_6_1_1 that the ePCO IE is used only when there is end-to-end support.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.20.4, Protocol configuration options; TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.1.1, General
results.model_answer: Include the Protocol configuration options (PCO) IE, not the Extended protocol configuration options (ePCO) IE.
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 6.6.1.1: ePCO shall be used only when supported end-to-end; otherwise PCO is used. Clause 8.3.20.4 states that for a UE in WB-S1 mode, with PDN Type other than non-IP/Ethernet and APN not for UAS services, the PCO IE shall be included when the UE wishes to transmit protocol data to the network.

results.question: If a UE in CS/PS mode 1 or 2 is already attached to both EPS and non-EPS services and needs to detach only from non-EPS services, what procedure must it use and what is the resulting EMM substate?
results.reference: The UE must perform a combined detach procedure for non-EPS services only (detach type 'IMSI detach'). This results in the UE entering the EMM-REGISTERED.IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED substate.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.5, Coordination between EMM and MM; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.4.9, EMM-REGISTERED.IMSI-DETACH-INITIATED
results.model_answer: It shall use the combined detach procedure with detach for non-EPS services only (IMSI detach). EPS registration is retained and the UE enters EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 5.1.5 and 5.5.2.2 (UE-initiated combined detach procedure).

results.question: During a tracking area update procedure, which message from the network provides the UE with EPS mobility management data, and under what condition does the UE respond with a TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE?
results.reference: The network sends the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message to provide the UE with EPS mobility management related data. The UE responds with a TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message if a GUTI has been changed or a new TMSI has been assigned in the accept message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.1, Message definition; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.27, Tracking area update complete
results.model_answer: The network provides EPS mobility management data in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message. The UE responds with TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE when the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT contains a GUTI (including when acknowledging a received Negotiated IMSI offset); it also responds if a previously stored negotiated IMSI offset is deleted by omission of the Negotiated IMSI offset IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.4: "If the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message contained a GUTI, the UE shall return a TRACKING AREA UPDATE COMPLETE message ... to acknowledge the received GUTI or the received Negotiated IMSI offset IE." The same clause specifies the UE processing of mobility-management information received in TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT.

results.question: According to the specifications, under what conditions is the Extended Protocol Configuration Options IE used instead of the Protocol Configuration Options IE for exchanging data between the UE and the network?
results.reference: The Extended Protocol Configuration Options IE is used if it is supported by both the UE and the network end-to-end for the PDN connection. Otherwise, the Protocol Configuration Options IE is used. This rule is defined in clause 6.6.1.1 and is referenced by numerous individual IE definitions, such as those in Clause_8_3_1_2 and Clause_8_3_1_4, which specify the use of the PCO or ePCO IEs based on this end-to-end support condition.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.1.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.2, Protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The Extended Protocol Configuration Options IE shall be used for a PDN connection when it is supported end-to-end by both the UE and network; otherwise the Protocol Configuration Options IE is used. For UE determination, end-to-end support exists if the UE is in NB-S1 mode, the APN is for UAS services, the requested PDN type is Non-IP or Ethernet, or the network indicated support in the last ATTACH ACCEPT/TAU ACCEPT and has sent the Extended PCO IE in at least one EPS session-management message for that PDN connection. For MME determination, it exists under the corresponding first three conditions, or when the UE indicated support in the last ATTACH REQUEST/TAU REQUEST and the MME has received Extended PCO from the PDN GW for that connection. The PDN GW relies on the latest support indication received from the MME or S-GW.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, clause 6.6.1.1 (General): "If supported by the network and UE end-to-end for a PDN connection, protocol configuration options shall be exchanged via the extended protocol configuration options IE. Otherwise the protocol configuration options IE is used." See also clauses 8.3.1.4, 8.3.2.4, 8.3.4.3, 8.3.5.3, 8.3.6.15 and 8.3.7.6.

results.question: When must a UE include the Additional information requested IE, and when will the network respond with the Ciphering key data IE?
results.reference: The UE shall include the Additional information requested IE (Clause_8_2_4_23) if it supports ciphered broadcast assistance data and needs to obtain new ciphering keys for it. The network will include the Ciphering key data IE (Clause_8_2_1_21) if it needs to send ciphering key data to the UE for ciphered broadcast assistance data.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.23, Additional information requested; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.21, Ciphering key data
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the Additional information requested IE when it supports ciphered broadcast assistance data and needs new ciphering keys; it sets the CipherKey bit to request them. In a TAU, this is mandatory for applicable non-periodic cases (except case zb), and is specifically triggered by, e.g., entry to a TA where stored keys are not applicable or when key validity will expire before the next periodic TAU. The network responds by including the Ciphering key data IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT when it accepts/provides the requested ciphering keys.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 8.2.4.23 / 8.2.29.29 (Additional information requested IE: UE includes it if it supports ciphered broadcast assistance data and needs new ciphering keys); clause 5.5.3.2.2 (TAU request CipherKey-bit conditions). Most likely response reference: clause 5.5.3.2.4, Tracking area updating accept.

results.question: What is the purpose of the ESM message container information element, and what specific rule in clause 7.5.2 applies to its handling within certain EMM messages?
results.reference: The purpose of the ESM message container information element is to enable piggybacked transfer of a single ESM message within an EMM message. According to clause 7.5.2, no semantical or syntactical diagnosis other than presence and length shall be performed on the ESM message container information element in the ATTACH REQUEST, ATTACH ACCEPT, ATTACH COMPLETE and CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST messages.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.3.15, ESM message container; TS 24.301, Clause 7.5.2, EPS mobility management
results.model_answer: It enables piggybacked transport of one ESM message inside an EMM message; the embedded ESM message is encoded without an NAS security header. Clause 7.5.2 requires that, where permitted in the specified EMM messages, only a single ESM message container (hence one ESM message) is carried and its contents are handled as the embedded ESM message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.15 (purpose and no NAS security header); most likely clause 7.5.2 (ESM message-container transport/handling rule).

results.question: Under what conditions is a UE in the EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED substate allowed to initiate a tracking area updating procedure, and what is a specific abnormal case that would prevent the procedure from starting in WB-S1 mode?
results.reference: In the EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED substate, the UE is allowed to initiate a tracking area updating or combined tracking area updating procedure. According to Clause_5_5_3_2_6, in WB-S1 mode, if access is barred for 'originating signalling', the tracking area updating procedure shall not be started.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.4.6, EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: A UE in EMM-REGISTERED.UPDATE-NEEDED is still in EMM-REGISTERED; therefore, if operating in CS/PS mode 1 or 2, it shall initiate combined TAU when an applicable trigger exists (for example, the current TAI is not in its registered TAI list, subject to the stated exception), provided no applicable abnormal-case restriction such as T3346 applies. In WB-S1 mode, an abnormal case that prevents starting TAU is access being barred for "originating signalling"; the UE shall not start TAU until access is granted or it moves to a cell where it is granted.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 5.5.3.3.2: UE in EMM-REGISTERED in CS/PS mode 1/2 shall initiate combined TAU for the listed triggers, including current TAI outside the registered TAI list. Clause 5.5.3.2.6(a): in WB-S1 mode, if access is barred for "originating signalling", the tracking area updating procedure shall not be started.

results.question: What is the common purpose of the NBIFOM container as described in Clause 8.3.6.12 and Clause 8.3.7.5?
results.reference: In both Clause 8.3.6.12 and Clause 8.3.7.5, the NBIFOM container is described as an information element used to transfer information associated with network-based IP flow mobility, as specified in 3GPP S 24.161 [36].
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.6.12, NBIFOM container; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.5, NBIFOM container
results.model_answer: It provides a container for transferring Network-Based IP Flow Mobility (NBIFOM) information/parameters between the UE and network for a PDN connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 8.3.6.12 and 8.3.7.5 (NBIFOM container).

results.question: Which two Information Elements (IEs) are used to assign a GUTI to a UE, and in which specific procedures are they used?
results.reference: A GUTI can be assigned to a UE using the IE in Clause_8_2_1_2 during an attach or combined EPS/IMSI attach procedure, or using the IE in Clause_8_2_26_3, which does not specify a particular procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.2, GUTI; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.3, GUTI
results.model_answer: The two IEs are the GUTI IE (EPS mobile identity coded as a GUTI), used to assign/reallocate the UE’s primary GUTI in the attach, tracking area updating, and GUTI reallocation procedures; and the Additional GUTI IE, used to assign an additional GUTI in the attach and tracking area updating procedures when applicable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301 clauses 5.5.1.2.4 (ATTACH ACCEPT), 5.5.3.2.4 (TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT), and 5.4.1.4 (GUTI reallocation procedure); message IE definitions in clause 8.

results.question: According to the specifications, what are the two optional IEs related to network naming that can be provided to the UE?
results.reference: The two optional IEs are: one to assign a new full name for network (Clause 8.2.19.7) and one to assign a new short name for network (Clause 8.2.19.8).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.7, Full name for network; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.8, Short name for network
results.model_answer: The two optional network-naming IEs are the Full name for network IE and the Short name for network IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 9.11.3 (Full name for network IE and Short name for network IE); most likely carried as optional IEs in the 5GS Network Feature Support / registration-related NAS information context.

results.question: What are the input parameters to the NAS ciphering algorithm when applying initial NAS message protection to a REGISTRATION REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST message?
results.reference: The input parameters are the BEARER ID, DIRECTION bit, NAS COUNT, NAS encryption key, and the length of the key stream to be generated by the encryption algorithm. The length of the key stream is set to the length of the entire plain NAS message that is included in the NAS message container IE, i.e., the value part of the NAS message container IE, that is to be ciphered.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.3.4, Ciphering and deciphering; TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.6, Protection of initial NAS signalling messages
results.model_answer: The NAS ciphering algorithm inputs are: BEARER ID, DIRECTION bit, NAS COUNT, NAS encryption key, and the key-stream length. For initial NAS message protection of a REGISTRATION REQUEST or SERVICE REQUEST, the key-stream length is the length of the entire plain NAS message carried in the NAS message container IE (i.e. the value part of that IE to be ciphered).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4.3.4 (Ciphering and deciphering).

results.question: Under what conditions can the AMF initiate a security mode control procedure to change the uplink NAS COUNT used in the latest SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message?
results.reference: The network may initiate the security mode control procedure in order to change the value of uplink NAS COUNT used in the latest SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message as described in 3GPP TS 33.501, subclause 6.9.4.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The AMF may initiate the NAS security mode control procedure in order to change the value of the uplink NAS COUNT used in the latest SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message. This is an explicitly permitted purpose of the procedure; no additional condition is specified in TS 24.501 beyond the AMF/network deciding to perform that change.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.2.1 (General), item b): the network may initiate security mode control "in order to change the value of uplink NAS COUNT used in the latest SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message" (with the related mechanism referenced to TS 33.501, clause 6.9.4.4).

results.question: What must a UE do to request the use of MICO mode, and under what conditions must the network include the MICO indication IE in response?
results.reference: The UE may include the MICO indication IE to request the use of MICO mode. The network shall include the MICO indication IE if the UE included the MICO indication IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message and the network supports and accepts the use of MICO mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.10, MICO indication; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.13, MICO indication
results.model_answer: The UE may request MICO mode by including the MICO indication IE in a REGISTRATION REQUEST message during a registration procedure. The UE shall not request MICO over non-3GPP access, nor during the specified emergency-related registration procedures. The network shall include the MICO indication IE in its registration response only when the UE included that IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST and the network supports and accepts MICO mode.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 8.2.6.10 (UE MICO indication IE), 8.2.7.13 (network inclusion rule), and 5.3.6 (MICO request restrictions).

results.question: According to the clauses, what are the two main purposes of the de-registration procedure when initiated by the UE?
results.reference: The de-registration procedure is used by the UE to de-register for 5GS services over 3GPP access when the UE is registered over 3GPP access, and to de-register for 5GS services over non-3GPP access when the UE is registered over non-3GPP access.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.2.3, UE-initiated de-registration procedure completion for 5GS services over 3GPP access
results.model_answer: When initiated by the UE, the de-registration procedure is used to de-register the UE from 5GS services over the applicable access: 3GPP access, non-3GPP access, or both accesses when registered in the same PLMN. It is also invoked by the UE for switch-off, eCall inactivity, or USIM removal as applicable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.2.1 (General), items a)-c) and UE invocation conditions a)-c).

results.question: Under what conditions must the network include the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE in a registration accept message, and what is a key restriction on the UE's use of eDRX?
results.reference: The network shall include the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE if the UE included the Requested extended DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message and the network supports eDRX and accepts the use of eDRX. The UE shall use eDRX only if it received the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE during the last registration procedure and the UE does not have an emergency PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.27, Negotiated extended DRX parameters; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.16, Extended DRX cycle for UEs in 5GMM-IDLE and 5GMM-CONNECTED mode with RRC inactive indication
results.model_answer: The network shall include the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE in REGISTRATION ACCEPT only when the UE included the Requested extended DRX parameters IE in REGISTRATION REQUEST and the network supports and accepts eDRX. The UE shall use eDRX only if it received the Negotiated extended DRX parameters IE during the last registration procedure and does not have an emergency PDU session.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.7.27; clause 5.3.16; and clause 5.5.1.2.4 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT handling): 'only if the Requested extended DRX parameters IE was included ... and the AMF supports and accepts the use of eDRX'; 'UE shall use eDRX only if it received ... during the last registration procedure and ... does not have an emergency PDU session.'

results.question: Which IEs can be included to assign a new 5G-GUTI to the UE?
results.reference: The 5G-GUTI IE may be included to assign a 5G-GUTI to a UE (Clause_8_2_7_2). The 5G-GUTI IE may also be included to assign a new 5G GUTI to the UE (Clause_8_2_19_3).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.2, 5G-GUTI; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.3, 5G-GUTI
results.model_answer: The 5G-GUTI IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message and in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message can be included to assign a (new) 5G-GUTI to the UE.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clauses 8.2.7.2 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT—5G-GUTI IE: may be included to assign a 5G-GUTI) and 8.2.19.3 (CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND—5G-GUTI IE: may be included to assign a new 5G-GUTI).

results.question: Under what two conditions related to disaster scenarios might the network include specific IEs to assign wait ranges to the UE?
results.reference: The network may include the 'Disaster roaming wait range' IE to assign a new disaster roaming wait range to the UE (Clause_8_2_7_45). The network may also include the 'Disaster return wait range' IE to assign a new disaster return wait range to the UE (Clause_8_2_7_46).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.45, Disaster roaming wait range; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.46, Disaster return wait range
results.model_answer: The network may include: (1) a Disaster roaming wait range IE when assigning a new wait range for UE registration on a PLMN offering disaster roaming while the UE's determined PLMN is under a disaster condition; and (2) a Disaster return wait range IE when assigning a new wait range for the UE to return/register after the disaster condition has ended.
results.evidence: TS 24.501 clause 4.24 (MINT): disaster roaming wait range applies upon selecting a PLMN for disaster roaming; disaster return wait range applies upon determining that the disaster condition has ended. See also clauses 8.2.7.45 and 8.2.19.29 (Disaster roaming wait range IE), and clauses 8.2.7.46, 8.2.9.8, 8.2.14.7 and 8.2.18.7 (Disaster return wait range IE): each IE may be included to assign a new respective wait range.

results.question: In which procedures can the network provision a 'CAG information list' to the UE, and what is a key purpose of this list in the context of PNI-NPN access?
results.reference: The network can provision a 'CAG information list' to the UE via the generic UE configuration update procedure, the registration procedure, the service request procedure, and the network-initiated de-registration procedure (Clause_4_14_3). A key purpose of this list in PNI-NPN is to prevent UEs not allowed to access a PNI-NPN from accessing it (Clause_4_14_3).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.14.3, Public network integrated non-public network (PNI-NPN); TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.36, CAG information list
results.model_answer: The network can provision a CAG information list via the generic UE configuration update procedure, registration procedure, service request procedure, and network-initiated de-registration procedure. For a PNI-NPN, the list supports CAG-based selection/access control: it identifies allowed CAG(s) and can indicate that the UE is permitted to access 5GS only via CAG cells, thereby preventing unauthorized UE access to the PNI-NPN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.14.3 (PNI-NPN): explicitly lists the four provisioning procedures and states that a CAG may be used to prevent UEs not allowed to access a PNI-NPN from accessing it. Supporting procedure-specific references: clauses 5.5.1.2.5, 5.5.1.3.5, and 5.6.1.5 for CAG information list in REGISTRATION REJECT/SERVICE REJECT; initial-registration acceptance behavior is in clause 5.5.1.2.4.

results.question: Which IEs can be included to assign a new TAI list to the UE?
results.reference: The TAI list IE may be included to assign a TAI list to a UE (Clause_8_2_7_4). The TAI list IE may also be included to assign a new TAI list to the UE (Clause_8_2_19_4).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.4, TAI list; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.4, TAI list
results.model_answer: The TAI list IE can be included in both the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message and the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message to assign a new TAI list to the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 8.2.7.4 (TAI list in REGISTRATION ACCEPT: "assign a TAI list to a UE") and 8.2.19.4 (TAI list in CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND: "assign a new TAI list to the UE").

results.question: When a UE camps on a satellite NG-RAN cell and receives multiple TACs, how does it select a TAI if no TAI belongs to its current registration area? What lists does the UE store for forbidden tracking areas when not operating in SNPN access operation mode?
results.reference: If no TAI belongs to the current registration area of the UE and there is a TAI which belongs to neither the list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming' nor the list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service', the UE shall select such a TAI. When not operating in SNPN access operation mode, the UE shall store a list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming', as well as a list of '5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.23.5, Handling multiple tracking area codes from the lower layers; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.13, Lists of 5GS forbidden tracking areas
results.model_answer: If no constructed TAI belongs to the current registration area, the UE first selects a TAI that belongs to neither the "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming" list nor the "5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service" list. If multiple such TAIs exist, it applies the allowed/non-allowed tracking-area selection rules used for TAIs in the registration area. If every TAI is in either forbidden list, all TAIs are considered equal and one is selected implementation-specifically. When not operating in SNPN access operation mode, the UE stores both a list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for roaming" and a list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.23.5, item b)1)-2) (multiple-TAC satellite NG-RAN TAI selection); clause 5.3.13, first paragraph (forbidden-TAI lists stored outside SNPN access operation mode).

results.question: Which clause specifies a capability related to UAV flight authorization, and which clause specifies an IE inclusion based on operator policy?
results.reference: Clause 4.22.4 states that the 5GS supports USS authorization of UAV flight. Clause 8.2.7.23 states that the NSSAI inclusion mode IE shall be included if required by operator policy.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.22.4, Authorization of UAV flight; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.23, NSSAI inclusion mode
results.model_answer: UAV flight authorization capability is specified in TS 24.501 clause 4.22.4 ("Authorization of UAV flight"). An IE inclusion based on operator policy is specified in clause 5.5.1.2.4: the AMF shall include the NSSAI inclusion mode IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message if required by operator policy.
results.evidence: Clause 4.22.4: "The 5GS supports USS authorization of UAV flight." Clause 5.5.1.2.4: "If required by operator policy, the AMF shall include the NSSAI inclusion mode IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message."

results.question: When does the UE include the 'Extended protocol configuration options' IE, and when does the network include its counterpart?
results.reference: The UE includes the 'Extended protocol configuration options' IE in a message when it needs to transmit (protocol) data (e.g., configuration parameters, error codes) to the network (Clause_8_3_1_9). The network includes the 'Extended protocol configuration options' IE in a message when it needs to transmit (protocol) data to the UE (Clause_8_3_3_5).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.9, Extended protocol configuration options; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.3.5, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The UE includes the Extended protocol configuration options IE when it needs to transmit protocol data (e.g. configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events) to the network. The network includes the counterpart IE when it needs to transmit such protocol data to the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 8.3.5.2 (UE-to-network EPCO) and 8.3.4.2 (network-to-UE EPCO).

results.question: Which two IEs can be included to assign new network names to the UE, and what is the distinction between them?
results.reference: The IE in Clause 8.2.19.7 can be included to assign a new full name for network to the UE. The IE in Clause 8.2.19.8 can be included to assign a new short name for network to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.7, Full name for network; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.8, Short name for network
results.model_answer: The two IEs are the Full name for network IE and the Short name for network IE. The Full name for network IE provides the complete operator/network name; the Short name for network IE provides an abbreviated network name for display where a shorter form is appropriate.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (Registration accepted by the network): the network may include the Full name for network IE and/or the Short name for network IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message.

results.question: Under what condition does a UE transition from the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE substate to the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION substate, and what is the general definition of the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state?
results.reference: A UE transitions from 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION if it receives a request from upper layers to establish an eCall over IMS or a call to an HPLMN designated non-emergency MSISDN/URI for test or terminal reconfiguration service. In the state 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, no 5GMM context has been established or the 5GMM context is marked as deregistered. The UE is deregistered.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.3.7, eCALL-INACTIVE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.3.2, 5GMM-DEREGISTERED
results.model_answer: The UE transitions from 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION when upper layers request establishment of either: (1) an eCall over IMS, or (2) a call to an HPLMN-designated non-emergency MSISDN or URI for test or terminal-reconfiguration service. 5GMM-DEREGISTERED is the 5GMM state entered, inter alia, following UE/network deregistration, registration or service-request rejection, UE switch-on, or expiry of the periodic registration-update timer for a UE registered for emergency services in 5GMM-IDLE; UE behavior is determined by its applicable DEREGISTERED substate.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 5.2.2.3.7 (5GMM-DEREGISTERED.eCALL-INACTIVE), exit conditions d) and e); clause 5.2.2.1 (General), definition/entry conditions of 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include both the Mobile station classmark 2 and Supported codecs IEs?
results.reference: Both IEs shall be included if the UE supports 5G-SRVCC from NG-RAN to UTRAN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.25, Mobile station classmark 2; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.26, Supported codecs
results.model_answer: In a REGISTRATION REQUEST, a UE supporting 5G-SRVCC from NG-RAN to UTRAN shall include both the Mobile station classmark 2 IE and the Supported codecs IE: (1) for initial registration; and (2) for mobility registration updating, for every trigger except when periodic registration updating (case b: T3512 expiry in 5GMM-IDLE) is the only reason for the update. The Mobile station classmark 2 IE itself is specified as included when the UE supports this 5G-SRVCC capability.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 5.5.1.2.2 (initial registration initiation: SRVCC-capable UE shall include Mobile station classmark 2 and Supported codecs) and 5.5.1.3.2 (mobility/periodic registration update: include both for all cases except case b); clause 8.2.6.25 (Mobile station classmark 2 IE included if UE supports 5G-SRVCC from NG-RAN to UTRAN).

results.question: Under what condition is the 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service"' IE included in a message, and what is the UE's behavior regarding the 'extended local emergency numbers list' when receiving a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message via non-3GPP access from a PLMN in a different country?
results.reference: The 'Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas for regional provision of service"' IE is included only if the message is sent via satellite NG-RAN access. When a REGISTRATION ACCEPT message is received via non-3GPP access from a PLMN in a country different from the current country of the UE, the UE shall keep the stored extended local emergency numbers list, if available.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.14.10, Forbidden TAI(s) for the list of "5GS forbidden tracking areas forregional provision of service"; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.12, Handling of local emergency numbers
results.model_answer: The AMF includes this IE in a SERVICE ACCEPT when it has received a list of TAIs from satellite NG-RAN and determines that any, but not all, of those TAIs are forbidden for regional provision of service (based on UDM information and operator choice). If a REGISTRATION ACCEPT is received via non-3GPP access from a PLMN in a country different from the UE's current country, the UE keeps its stored extended local emergency numbers list, if available.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 5.6.1.4.1: satellite NG-RAN partial forbidden-TAI handling and inclusion of the Forbidden TAI(s) IE in SERVICE ACCEPT. TS 24.501, clause 5.3.12 (with 5.3.12A conditions): UE keeps the stored local and extended local emergency numbers lists when REGISTRATION ACCEPT via non-3GPP access is from a PLMN in a different country.

results.question: What integrity protection applies when the network provides a Payload container IE with the type set to 'SOR transparent container' in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message, and in which specific NAS message from the UE is the PDU session ID IE mandated when carrying 'N1 SM information'?
results.reference: When the network provides a Payload container IE with the Payload container type IE set to 'SOR transparent container' in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message, the Payload container IE is integrity protected by the HPLMN or subscribed SNPN. The UE shall include the PDU session ID IE in the UL NAS TRANSPORT message when the Payload container type IE is set to 'N1 SM information'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.7, Protection of NAS IEs; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.10.2, PDU session ID
results.model_answer: For a DL NAS TRANSPORT with Payload container type "SOR transparent container", the UE/ME processes the container only if it successfully passes the integrity check specified in TS 33.501; otherwise it discards the container contents. For UE-originated "N1 SM information", the PDU session ID IE is mandated in the UL NAS TRANSPORT message.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 5.4.5.3.3(d): SOR transparent container is processed only upon successful integrity check (TS 33.501); on failure, contents are discarded. TS 24.501, clause 5.4.5.2.2(a): for UE-initiated N1 SM information in UL NAS TRANSPORT, the UE shall set the PDU session ID IE to the PDU session ID.

results.question: According to the specifications, when a UE has a valid 5G NAS security context and needs to send non-cleartext IEs in a REGISTRATION REQUEST message, how should the message be protected?
results.reference: The UE includes the entire REGISTRATION REQUEST message (i.e. containing both cleartext IEs and non-cleartext IEs) in the NAS message container IE, ciphers the value part of the NAS message container IE, and then sends a REGISTRATION REQUEST message containing the cleartext IEs and the NAS message container IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.6, Protection of initial NAS signalling messages; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.21, NAS message container
results.model_answer: The UE shall place the entire REGISTRATION REQUEST (both cleartext and non-cleartext IEs) in the NAS message container IE, cipher the value part of that IE, and transmit an outer REGISTRATION REQUEST containing the cleartext IEs plus the NAS message container IE. The outer initial NAS message shall use security header type "integrity protected".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.4.6, item b)1), and the subsequent requirement: an initial NAS message including a NAS message container IE shall have security header type set to "integrity protected".

results.question: How does the UE determine the RRC establishment cause for non-3GPP access, and what is the role of access identities in this process?
results.reference: When establishment of an N1 NAS signalling connection over non-3GPP access is initiated, the UE shall determine one or more access identities to be associated with the establishment as specified in subclause 4.5.2 and table 4.5.2.1, and then select the establishment cause for non-3GPP access from the determined one or more access identities and the event which triggered the initiation by checking the rules specified in table 4.7.2.2.1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.7.2.2, Establishment cause for non-3GPP access; TS 24.301, Clause 4.5.2, Determination of the access identities and access category associated with a request for access for UEs not operating in SNPN access mode
results.model_answer: For non-3GPP access, the UE does not select an RRC establishment cause. It selects an "establishment cause for non-3GPP access." Upon initiating an N1 NAS signalling connection, the UE: (1) determines one or more applicable access identities in accordance with clause 4.5.2 and table 4.5.2.1; (2) selects the non-3GPP establishment cause by applying table 4.7.2.2.1 to those access identities and to the event that triggered the connection; and (3) provides the selected cause to lower layers. If multiple rules match, the lowest rule number takes precedence. Access identities are therefore inputs to the table-based cause selection; their use, including identities 0, 1, 2, and 11-15, is defined by clause 4.5.2/table 4.5.2.1. Possible causes include emergency, MO signalling, MO data, MO SMS, MO MMTel voice, and MO MMTel video.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.7.2.2 and table 4.7.2.2.1 (especially steps a)-c) and the lowest-rule-number rule); clause 4.5.2 and table 4.5.2.1 (determination/use of access identities).

results.question: A UE operating in single-registration mode performs an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode in 5GMM-IDLE mode. According to the coordination rules, what substates does the UE enter for 3GPP access and EMM, and what procedure does it subsequently initiate?
results.reference: The UE shall enter substates EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE and 5GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE for 3GPP access and then initiate the registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update over 3GPP access indicating "mobility registration updating" in the 5GS registration type IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4.3, Coordination between 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM without N26 interface; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.16, EPS NAS message container
results.model_answer: The UE enters 5GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE for 3GPP access and EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE. It then initiates a 5GS registration procedure for mobility and periodic registration update over 3GPP access, with the 5GS registration type set to "mobility registration updating" in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.4.3: at inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode in 5GMM-IDLE mode, a single-registration-mode UE enters EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE and 5GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE for 3GPP access, then initiates registration for mobility and periodic registration update indicating "mobility registration updating" (see clause 5.5.1.3).

results.question: Which IEs can be included to assign a new service area list to the UE?
results.reference: The Service area list IE may be included to assign new service area restrictions to the UE (Clause_8_2_7_15). The Service area list IE may also be included to assign a new service area list to the UE (Clause_8_2_19_6).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.15, Service area list; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.6, Service area list
results.model_answer: The Service area list IE can be included in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message and in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message to assign a new service area list to the UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 8.2.7.15 (Service area list IE in REGISTRATION ACCEPT) and 8.2.19.6 (Service area list IE in CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND). Clause 5.4.4.1 also identifies the Service area list as a parameter supported by generic UE configuration update.

results.question: When the AMF includes the Back-off timer value IE in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message, what specific condition related to the Payload container must be met, and what is the general purpose of the network-initiated NAS transport procedure that uses this message?
results.reference: The AMF includes the Back-off timer value IE when the Payload container IE contains an uplink 5GSM message which was not forwarded due to specified congestion or subscription issues, and the Payload container type IE is not set to 'Multiple payloads'. The purpose of the network-initiated NAS transport procedure is to provide transport of various payload types, including such non-forwarded 5GSM messages, from the AMF to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.11.5, Back-off timer value; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.5.3.1, General
results.model_answer: The Payload container shall carry the single uplink message that was not forwarded (a 5GSM message for N1 SM information, or CIoT user-data container for the CIoT case). The Back-off timer is included for congestion-control rejection (5GMM cause #22, #67, or #69); it may also be included with cause #91 when the DNN is unsupported in the slice. The network-initiated NAS transport procedure enables the AMF to deliver network-originated payloads, including returned/unforwarded uplink payloads and their failure/congestion indication, to the UE in a DL NAS TRANSPORT message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.5.3.2, cases e), f), l2): the AMF sets the Payload container to the message/container 'which was not forwarded' and includes the Back-off timer value IE for congestion causes #22/#67/#69 (optional for cause #91 in the stated DNN-not-supported-in-slice case). Clause 5.4.5.3.2: in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode, the AMF initiates network-initiated NAS transport by sending DL NAS TRANSPORT.

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include the EPS NAS message container in a REGISTRATION REQUEST message during an initial registration procedure?
results.reference: The UE performing initial registration shall include the EPS NAS message container if: 1) it was previously registered in S1 mode before entering state EMM-DEREGISTERED; and 2) it has received an "interworking without N26 interface not supported" indication from the network; and b) EPS security context and a valid 4G-GUTI are available. The content is the complete integrity protected ATTACH REQUEST message, using EPS security context.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.16, EPS NAS message container; TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.2.1, General
results.model_answer: During initial registration, the UE shall include the EPS NAS message container IE when it was previously registered in S1 mode before entering EMM-DEREGISTERED, has received an "interworking without N26 interface not supported" indication from the network, and an EPS security context plus a valid native 4G-GUTI are available. The container carries the complete integrity-protected ATTACH REQUEST, protected using the EPS security context.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (Initial registration initiation); clause 8.2.6.16 (EPS NAS message container).

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include the Service-level-AA container IE in a message, and which specific messages require it?
results.reference: The UE shall include the Service-level-AA container IE if the UE supporting UAS services requests a registration for UAS services (Clause_8_2_6_35). Furthermore, this IE shall be included in the message when the UE needs to establish a PDU session for the UAS services (Clause_8_3_1_16).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.35, Service-level-AA container; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.16, Service-level-AA container
results.model_answer: A UE supporting UAS services shall include the Service-level-AA container IE in a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST when it requests establishment of a PDU session for C2 communication/UAS services. It shall include the service-level device ID set to its CAA-level UAV ID; for C2 communication, it also includes the C2 authorization payload and payload type when available. For a UAS-services request initiated on upper-layer request, the USS address and UUAA payload/type are included when provided by upper layers. During a DN-initiated service-level-AA procedure, when upper layers provide a service-level-AA payload in response to SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND, the UE shall include that payload in the Service-level-AA container IE of a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 6.4.1.2 (UE-requested PDU session establishment: mandatory Service-level-AA container for UAS/C2 requests) and 6.3.1A.3 (UE creates SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE and sets the Service-level-AA container payload).

results.question: What is the fundamental difference in context management between a UE operating in single-registration mode and one operating in dual-registration mode when both 5GMM and EMM are enabled?
results.reference: If both 5GMM and EMM are enabled, a UE operating in single-registration mode shall maintain one common registration for 5GMM for 3GPP access and EMM. In contrast, a UE operating in the dual-registration mode shall maintain independent contexts for 5GMM and EMM, which includes independent lists of equivalent PLMNs.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.3, Dual-registration mode
results.model_answer: In single-registration mode, the UE shall maintain one common registration for 5GMM over 3GPP access and EMM, with coordination between them as specified. In dual-registration mode, the UE shall maintain independent 5GMM and EMM contexts, including independent equivalent-PLMN lists; coordination is generally not needed except for explicitly specified cases.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.1.4.1 (General) and clause 4.8.3 (Dual-registration mode).

results.question: What is the relationship between mapped EPS bearer contexts and QoS rules in an MA PDU session, and what action does the UE take regarding mapped EPS bearer contexts?
results.reference: In an MA PDU session, the UE shall have one set of the mapped EPS bearer contexts, and the network can provide this set via either access of the MA PDU session (Clause_6_1_4_1). The UE can request to delete one or more mapped EPS bearer contexts by including the Mapped EPS bearer contexts IE in a message (Clause_8_3_7_10).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.4.1, Coordination between 5GSM and ESM with N26 interface; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.10, Mapped EPS bearer contexts
results.model_answer: In an MA PDU session, the UE maintains one common set of mapped EPS bearer contexts, which the network may provide via either access. The UE shall support their modification or deletion via either access, irrespective of whether the context was created via the same or the other access. Mapped EPS bearer contexts are associated with QoS flows; consequently, the QoS rule(s) and QoS-flow description(s) for those flows are associated with the corresponding EPS bearer context. If mapped EPS bearer contexts exist but none is associated with the default QoS rule, the UE shall locally delete all mapped EPS bearer contexts and remove the stored EBI from all QoS-flow descriptions of that PDU session.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.1.4.1 (Coordination between 5GSM and ESM with N26 interface): MA PDU session has one set of mapped EPS bearer contexts; network may provide it via either access; UE supports modification/deletion through either access. Also see clauses 6.3.2.3 and 6.4.1.3 for the requirement to locally delete mapped EPS bearer contexts when none is associated with the default QoS rule.

results.question: What are two events that cause a UE to enter the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state, and what is the purpose of the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION substate?
results.reference: Two events that cause a UE to enter the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state are: a) the de-registration is performed either by the UE or by the network, and b) the registration request is rejected by the AMF. The substate 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION is chosen in the UE if the initial registration procedure failed due to a missing response from the network or due to specific error circumstances.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.1.3.4, 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION
results.model_answer: Examples: (1) completion of a de-registration procedure (e.g. after a network-initiated DEREGISTRATION REQUEST); and (2) failure or rejection of an initial registration procedure. The 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION substate indicates that valid subscriber data exist but an initial registration is required and the UE is attempting/re-attempting it as soon as possible.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 5.1.3.2.1.3.4 (ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION is selected when initial registration fails due to no network response or specified registration-failure circumstances) and 5.2.2.4(d) (on return to 5GMM-DEREGISTERED, select ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION if initial registration is to be performed).

results.question: For which PDU session types is the 'Maximum number of supported packet filters' IE included in the message after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, and what is a key characteristic of the UE's operation mode and network interface in this scenario?
results.reference: The 'Maximum number of supported packet filters' IE shall be included in the message for a PDN connection established when in S1 mode, after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, if the UE is a UE operating in single-registration mode in a network supporting N26 interface, the PDU session type is "IPv4", "IPv6", "IPv4v6" or "Ethernet", and the UE can support more than 16 packet filters for this PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.4, Maximum number of supported packet filters; TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.2.2, Single-registration mode with N26 interface
results.model_answer: The IE is included for PDU session types IPv4, IPv6, IPv4v6, or Ethernet, provided the UE supports more than 16 packet filters and has not previously successfully reported this capability. The UE operates in single-registration mode and the network supports the N26 interface.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.3.7.4; see also clause 6.4.2.2.

results.question: What actions must a UE take regarding its N1 mode capability for 3GPP access when changing its usage setting from 'data centric' to 'voice centric' and IMS voice is not available over 3GPP access only?
results.reference: If the UE's usage setting changes from 'data centric' to 'voice centric' and 'IMS voice not available' over 3GPP access only, and if the UE is only registered over 3GPP access, the UE shall disable the N1 mode capability for 3GPP access as specified in subclause 4.9.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.3, Change of UE's usage setting; TS 24.301, Clause 4.9.2, Disabling and re-enabling of UE's N1 mode capability for 3GPP access
results.model_answer: In single-registration mode, if the UE is only registered over 3GPP access, it shall disable its N1 mode capability for 3GPP access and follow TS 24.501 subclause 4.9.2. If it has a persistent PDU session, it waits until the associated radio bearer is released before disabling. The specified table row does not require disabling 3GPP N1 capability when the UE is also registered over non-3GPP access and IMS voice is unavailable only over 3GPP access.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.3.3, Table 4.3.3.1: "From data centric to voice centric and IMS voice not available over 3GPP access only" -> "Disable the N1 mode capability for 3GPP access ... if the UE is only registered over 3GPP access (NOTE)." NOTE: wait for release of the radio bearer associated with a persistent PDU session. See also clause 4.3.2 and clause 4.9.2.

results.question: Under what conditions is the PDU address IE included in a message, and what specific IP address or identifier is included when the Selected PDU session type is IPv6?
results.reference: The PDU address IE is included when the selected PDU session type is "IPv4", "IPv6" or "IPv4v6". If the network sets the Selected PDU session type IE to IPv6, the network shall include an interface identifier for the IPv6 link local address in the PDU address IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.2.3, PDU address; TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.4.2, IP address allocation via NAS signalling
results.model_answer: In a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT message, the SMF shall include the PDU address IE when the selected PDU session type is IPv4, IPv6, or IPv4v6. For Selected PDU session type IPv6, it shall set the PDU address IE to the interface identifier allocated to the UE for its IPv6 link-local address (not the IPv6 prefix). For a PDU session established by a W-AGF on behalf of an FN-RG, the SMF shall additionally indicate its own IPv6 link-local address in that IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.3, 'UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure accepted by the network': 'If the selected PDU session type is "IPv6", the SMF shall include the PDU address IE ... and shall set the PDU address IE to an interface identifier for the IPv6 link local address allocated to the UE.' See also clause 6.2.4.2(c) and clause 6.2.4.1.

results.question: In which two scenarios does a UE indicate its support for a multi-homed IPv6 PDU session, and what is a prerequisite regarding the PDU session type for these indications?
results.reference: The UE indicates support of the multi-homed IPv6 PDU session 1) during the UE-requested PDU session establishment of a PDU session of "IPv6" or "IPv4v6" PDU session type; and 2) during the UE-requested PDU session modification performed after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, for a PDU session associated with a PDN connection established when in S1 mode, if the UE is a UE operating in single-registration mode in a network supporting N26 interface, the PDU session is of "IPv6" or "IPv4v6" PDU session type, and the UE has not previously successfully performed the UE-requested PDU session modification to provide this indication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.11, Multi-homed IPv6 PDU session; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.2, 5GSM capability
results.model_answer: A UE indicates support for a multi-homed IPv6 PDU session: (1) during UE-requested PDU session establishment; and (2) during UE-requested PDU session modification after an inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode for a PDU session associated with a PDN connection established in S1 mode (single-registration mode, N26-supported network, and the indication not previously successfully provided). In both scenarios, the PDU session type shall be IPv6 or IPv4v6.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.2.11, items b)1 and b)2. For the modification signalling detail, see clause 6.4.2.2: MH6-PDU is set in the 5GSM capability IE for an IPv6 or IPv4v6 PDU session.

results.question: If a UE wants to use or change its UE-specific DRX parameters, what must it include in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message? What is the corresponding condition for the network to include the Negotiated DRX parameters IE?
results.reference: If the UE wants to use or change the UE specific DRX parameters, the UE shall include the Requested DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message. The network shall include the Negotiated DRX parameters IE if the Requested DRX parameters IE was included in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.15, Requested DRX parameters; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.25, Negotiated DRX parameters
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the Requested DRX parameters IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST. The network shall include the Negotiated DRX parameters IE if the UE included the Requested DRX parameters IE and the network supports and accepts use of UE-specific DRX parameters.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.6.15 (Requested DRX parameters); most likely corresponding clause 8.2.7.26 (Negotiated DRX parameters).

results.question: What action does the AMF take if timer T3560 expires for the first time during an EAP-based authentication procedure, and what is the consequence if it expires for the fifth time?
results.reference: On the first expiry of timer T3560, the AMF shall retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and shall reset and start timer T3560. On the fifth expiry of timer T3560, the AMF shall abort the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure and any ongoing 5GMM specific procedure, and release the N1 NAS signalling connection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: On the first expiry of T3560, the AMF retransmits the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message and resets/restarts T3560. This is repeated four times; on the fifth expiry, the AMF aborts the EAP-based primary authentication and key agreement procedure and any ongoing 5GMM-specific procedure, and releases the N1 NAS signalling connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.4.4(a) (Abnormal cases on the network side): first T3560 expiry requires retransmission and restart; fifth expiry requires aborting EAP-based primary authentication/key agreement and ongoing 5GMM procedure, and releasing the N1 NAS signalling connection.

results.question: What are two IEs that must be included based on the UE's support for specific voice-related capabilities?
results.reference: The UE's usage setting IE shall be included if the UE supports IMS voice. The Mobile station classmark 2 IE shall be included if the UE supports 5G-SRVCC from NG-RAN to UTRAN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.14, UE's usage setting; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.25, Mobile station classmark 2
results.model_answer: There are not two distinct IEs: both capabilities are indicated in the 5GS network feature support IE of REGISTRATION ACCEPT. If accepted, the AMF sets the N1 NAS signalling connection release bit and the paging indication for voice services bit, respectively.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.3.4: the AMF shall set the N1 NAS signalling connection release bit and, when accepted, the paging indication for voice services bit in the 5GS network feature support IE of REGISTRATION ACCEPT.

results.question: What information elements may be included to update the UE's network identifiers, and what specific type of name does each provide?
results.reference: Two IEs may be included: one provides a new full name for the network (Clause 8.2.19.7), and the other provides a new short name for the network (Clause 8.2.19.8).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.7, Full name for network; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.8, Short name for network
results.model_answer: The CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND may include the Full name for network IE, providing the network's full (long) name, and the Short name for network IE, providing the network's short name.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.4.1 (CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message content); see also clause 5.4.4.2 for the generic UE configuration update procedure.

results.question: What triggers the network to send NSAG information, and what does the UE provide to its lower layers along with this information?
results.reference: The network may include the NSAG information IE if the UE has set the NSAG bit to 'NSAG supported' in the 5GMM capability IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message. Along with the NSAG information, the UE provides to the lower layers with allowed NSSAI and requested NSSAI for the purpose of NSAG-aware cell reselection.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.34, NSAG information; TS 24.301, Clause 4.6.2.6, Provision of NSAG information to lower layers
results.model_answer: The network may send NSAG information when the UE has indicated "NSAG supported" by setting the NSAG bit in the 5GMM capability IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message. If NSAG information is available, the UE NAS provides the most recent NSAG information to lower layers, together with the allowed NSSAI and requested NSSAI for NSAG-aware cell reselection.
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 8.2.19.34 (NSAG information); clause 4.6.2.6 (Provision of NSAG information to lower layers).

results.question: Under what condition does the AUSF or AAA server send an EAP-request/AKA'-notification message after receiving an EAP-response/AKA'-challenge, and what is the UE's required action upon receiving that notification?
results.reference: The AUSF or AAA server sends an EAP-request/AKA'-notification message if procedures for handling the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message are not successful. Upon receiving an EAP-request/AKA'-notification message, the UE shall send an EAP-response/AKA'-notification message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.9, Network not successfully authenticates UE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.6, UE handling EAP-AKA' notification message
results.model_answer: After successful handling of the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge, the AUSF or AAA server sends an EAP-request/AKA'-notification when it included AT_RESULT_IND in the EAP-request/AKA'-challenge and the UE also included AT_RESULT_IND in the corresponding EAP-response/AKA'-challenge. Upon receiving this notification, the UE shall handle it as specified in RFC 5448 and send an EAP-response/AKA'-notification message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.2.5 (Network successfully authenticates UE): condition for sending EAP-request/AKA'-notification. UE handling is specified in the corresponding UE-side EAP-AKA' notification procedure in clause 5.4.1.2.1, with EAP-AKA' message processing per RFC 5448.

results.question: Under what condition does the network provide NSAG information to the UE, and what must the UE NAS layer do if it receives this information?
results.reference: The network may include the NSAG information IE if the UE has set the NSAG bit to 'NSAG supported' in the 5GMM capability IE of the REGISTRATION REQUEST message. If NSAG information is available, the UE NAS layer shall provide the lower layers with the most recent NSAG information.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.51, NSAG information; TS 24.301, Clause 4.6.2.6, Provision of NSAG information to lower layers
results.model_answer: The network provides NSAG information to the UE in the NSAG information IE of a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message. Upon receipt, the UE shall store the NSAG information as specified in subclause 4.6.2.2; if NSAG information is available, the UE NAS layer shall provide the lower layers with the most recent NSAG information (together with allowed NSSAI and requested NSSAI for NSAG-aware cell reselection).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4.3: "If the UE receives the NSAG information IE in the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND message, the UE shall store the NSAG information as specified in subclause 4.6.2.2." Clause 4.6.2.6: "If NSAG information is available, the UE NAS layer shall provide the lower layers with the most recent NSAG information."

results.question: What are the conditions for including the 5GSM cause IE in a message, and what is a specific example of its use when a UE rejects a network request?
results.reference: The 5GSM cause IE is included in the message to indicate the reason for the deletion of one or more non-default QoS rules, QoS flow descriptions or mapped EPS bearer contexts (Clause_8_3_7_3). A specific example is when a UE rejects a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND message; in this case, the UE shall create a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND REJECT message and set the 5GSM cause IE to indicate the reason for rejecting the PDU session modification (Clause_6_3_2_4).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.7.3, 5GSM cause; TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.2.4, Network-requested PDU session modification procedure not accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The 5GSM cause IE is included when a 5GSM message rejects a request or otherwise needs to indicate the reason for failure/release; where specified, its value shall identify that reason. For example, if a UE cannot accept a network-requested PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND, it sends a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT including the 5GSM cause IE, e.g. cause #26 "insufficient resources" (or another applicable rejection cause).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.3.2.3.2 (UE handling of network-requested PDU session modification); see also clause 6.4.1.4.1 (PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT: SMF shall set 5GSM cause IE to indicate the rejection reason) and clause 6.3.3.2 (PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND: SMF shall set 5GSM cause IE to indicate the release reason).

results.question: What are the network's paging restrictions for a UE with downlink user data pending, and how does the paging procedure relate to the establishment of a NAS signalling connection?
results.reference: If the network has downlink user data pending for a UE and the AMF has stored paging restriction, the network should not page the UE if the Paging restriction type is set to 'All paging is restricted'. It should page only for voice service if set to 'All paging is restricted except for voice service', and only for specified PDU sessions or voice service if set accordingly. The paging procedure is performed in 3GPP access and is used by the network to request the establishment of a NAS signalling connection to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.2.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.1, General
results.model_answer: For downlink user data pending, if the AMF has stored paging restriction: (1) "All paging is restricted": the network should not page; (2) "All paging is restricted except for voice service": page only if the pending data is voice-service-related; (3) "All paging is restricted except for specified PDU session(s)": page only if pending data is for a PDU session not restricted by the stored restriction; (4) "All paging is restricted except for voice service and specified PDU session(s)": page only for voice-related data or for an unrestricted PDU session. Paging is performed only over 3GPP access and is used by the network to request establishment of a NAS signalling connection to the UE; it is also used to request re-establishment of user-plane resources for downlink data, including PDU sessions associated with non-3GPP access over 3GPP access.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.2.2.1 (network paging initiation and paging-restriction rules for pending downlink user data); clause 5.6.2.1 (paging is only in 3GPP access and requests establishment of a NAS signalling connection).

results.question: What message does a UE acting as a relay send to initiate the remote UE report procedure, and what must the UE do if timer T3586 expires for the first time after sending this message?
results.reference: The UE initiates the procedure by creating and sending a REMOTE UE REPORT message. If timer T3586 expires for the first time, the UE shall resend the REMOTE UE REPORT message and shall reset and restart timer T3586.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.2, Remote UE report procedure initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.4, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The relay UE sends a REMOTE UE REPORT message to initiate the 5G ProSe remote UE report procedure. If T3586 expires for the first time, the UE shall resend the REMOTE UE REPORT message, then reset and restart T3586.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.6.2.2 (Remote UE report procedure initiation) and clause 6.6.2.4(a) (Abnormal cases in the UE).

results.question: What is the UE's behavior if it receives a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message for a PDU session it is currently releasing, and what IE is included if the service-level authentication fails with cause #29?
results.reference: If the UE receives a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message during the UE-requested PDU session release procedure for the same PDU session, it shall ignore the message and proceed with the release. If the service-level authentication and authorization procedure completes unsuccessfully with 5GSM cause #29, the network shall include the Service-level-AA container IE containing the service-level-AA response if provided by the DN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.1A.5, Abnormal cases in the UE; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.3.7, Service-level-AA container
results.model_answer: The UE shall ignore the SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND and continue the UE-requested PDU session release procedure. For a failed service-level authentication/authorization resulting in 5GSM cause #29, the PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND includes the Service-level-AA container IE containing the service-level-AA response, with SLAR set to "Service level authentication and authorization was not successful or service level authorization is revoked".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 6.3.1A.5 (collision with UE-requested PDU session release: UE ignores the command and proceeds with release) and 6.3.3.2 (UUAA-SM failure/revocation: PDU SESSION RELEASE COMMAND includes Service-level-AA container IE and 5GSM cause #29).

results.question: What message does the UE send to the AMF after receiving an EAP-request/AKA'-challenge message and successfully authenticating the network, and what does the AMF do upon receiving that message?
results.reference: The UE sends an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message containing an EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message. Upon receipt of the AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message, the AMF shall stop timer T3560.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.2.3, UE successfully authenticates network; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.1.2.4.3, EAP message reliable transport procedure accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE sends an AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message containing an EAP-response/AKA'-challenge message to the AMF. The AMF forwards the contained EAP response to the AUSF (or, as applicable, the AAA server of the CH/DCS) for EAP-AKA' authentication processing.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.1.2.2.3 (UE successfully authenticates network); see also clause 5.4.1.2.2.5 for network processing of the EAP-response/AKA'-challenge.

results.question: What action does the UE take upon receiving a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, and what is the purpose of the overall procedure?
results.reference: Upon receipt of a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, the UE passes to the upper layers the service-level-AA payload received in the Service-level-AA container IE. The purpose of the service-level authentication and authorization procedure is to enable the DN to authenticate and/or authorize the upper layers of the UE when establishing or after establishing a PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.1A.2, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.model_answer: Upon receiving a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message and PDU session ID via NAS transport, the UE passes the Service-level-AA container payload to its upper layers. The DN-initiated procedure is otherwise transparent to the UE 5GSM layer. When upper layers return a service-level-AA payload, the UE sends it in a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message with the PDU session ID using NAS transport. The overall procedure enables a DN using NEF services to authenticate and/or authorize UE upper layers during establishment of a non-emergency PDU session, or to re-authenticate them after PDU-session establishment.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 6.3.1A.1 (purpose and applicability of service-level-AA) and 6.3.1A.2-6.3.1A.3 (UE passes the received payload to upper layers and returns upper-layer payload in SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE via NAS transport).

results.question: In the UE, what is the state of a procedure transaction when it has been initiated towards the network, and what principle governs the inclusion of the PTI value in the initial request message?
results.reference: The state is 'PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING'. The principle governing the PTI inclusion is that when the UE initiates a transaction related procedure, it shall include a valid PTI value in the message header of the request message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.2.8, PROCEDURE TRANSACTION PENDING; TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.1, Principles of PTI handling for 5GSM procedures
results.model_answer: A UE-initiated procedure transaction is pending/outstanding toward the network until resolved. The UE shall include a valid, currently unused PTI in the header of the initial request message; responses/related commands reuse that PTI.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.2.1 (Principles of PTI handling for 5GSM procedures); for REMOTE UE REPORT specifically, clause 6.6.2.2.

results.question: During the registration procedure, how does a MUSIM UE indicate support for features, and what is the network's corresponding action regarding feature support indication?
results.reference: If a MUSIM UE supports one or more MUSIM features (except for the paging timing collision control), the UE indicates support of one or more MUSIM features during the registration procedure. If the network decides to accept one or more MUSIM features, it indicates the support of one or more MUSIM features during the registration procedure. The network only indicates support of the paging restriction together with support of either N1 NAS signalling connection release or the reject paging request.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.25, Support of MUSIM features; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.8, 5GS network feature support
results.model_answer: A MUSIM UE indicates support for one or more MUSIM features during registration, except paging timing collision control. If it indicates support for N1 NAS signalling connection release and/or reject paging request and also supports paging restriction, it also indicates paging-restriction support. If the network accepts one or more indicated MUSIM features, it indicates the accepted feature support during registration. The network may indicate paging-restriction support only together with support for N1 NAS signalling connection release and/or reject paging request; it shall not indicate any MUSIM feature during registration for emergency services.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 4.25 (Support of MUSIM features). For REGISTRATION ACCEPT bit-setting details, see clause 5.5.1.3.4 (Mobility and periodic registration update accepted by the network).

results.question: Which two messages are sent by the UE to the AMF to complete a registration procedure and a configuration update procedure, respectively?
results.reference: To complete a registration procedure, the UE sends the REGISTRATION COMPLETE message to the AMF. To complete a configuration update procedure, the UE sends the CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE message to the AMF.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.8.1, Message definition; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.20.1, Message definition
results.model_answer: REGISTRATION COMPLETE and CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE, respectively.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 5.5.1 (registration procedure completion via REGISTRATION COMPLETE) and 5.4.4.2 (generic UE configuration update procedure; UE acknowledgement via CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMPLETE).

results.question: What is the state of a procedure transaction when none exists, and what PTI value should be used in a command message that is not sent as a result of a received request message in such a context?
results.reference: The state is 'PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE'. In a command message not sent as a result of a received request message, the sending entity shall include the PTI value set to 'no procedure transaction identity assigned'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.2.7, PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE; TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.1, Principles of PTI handling for 5GSM procedures
results.model_answer: When no procedure transaction exists, it is in the PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE state. A command message not sent as a result of a received request message shall use the PTI value "no procedure transaction identity assigned".
results.evidence: TS 24.501, clause 6.2.1: a command message not sent as a result of a received request message shall include PTI set to "no procedure transaction identity assigned". The inactive transaction state is evidenced by procedure handling text (e.g. T3580 expiry) stating that, after release of the allocated PTI, the UE enters state PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE.

results.question: Under what condition is the Remote UE handling information list IE included in a message from the SMF to the UE during the remote UE report procedure, and what must the UE do upon receiving this IE?
results.reference: The SMF may include the Remote UE handling information IE if the PDU session authentication and authorization procedure for the 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE were performed. Upon receipt of the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE message including this IE, the UE shall pass the Remote UE handling information IE to the upper layer as defined in 3GPP TS 24.554.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.2.3, Remote UE report procedure accepted by the network; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.5.3, Remote UE handling information list
results.model_answer: The SMF may include the Remote UE handling information IE in the REMOTE UE REPORT RESPONSE if the PDU session authentication and authorization procedure for the 5G ProSe layer-3 remote UE was performed.
